value: minimum audible angle 4.9 deg (mean, SD 0.3) for broadband noise at 0 deg azimuth in the single-reference paradigm
method: behavioural Go/NoGo task: owls left a waiting perch to report a change in loudspeaker position; MAA taken as the angular separation at which d' reached 1.0 (cumulative normal fitted to psychometric functions, method of constant stimuli)
conditions: 3 European barn owls, hand-reared from about 12 days of age (two hatched at Oldenburg, one at Munich), all three completed all six stimulus types; stimuli 100 ms at 40 dB SPL with +/-3 dB level roving, narrowband noise (40 Hz bandwidth) at 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 and 8000 Hz plus broadband noise (500-8000 Hz); stimulus types tested in separate sessions in a sequence randomised per owl; reference fixed at 0 deg (frontal) in this paradigm; acuity differed significantly between stimulus types (F = 39.942, p < 0.001) and individual owls did not differ significantly; the smaller multiple-reference paradigm (two owls, references at -45, 0 and +45 deg) gave larger lateral MAAs than frontal ones; the Abstract's figures (14 deg at 500 Hz to 6 deg at 8000 Hz, about 4 deg for broadband) do not match this paradigm's Results (13.7 at 500 Hz, 8.4 at 8000 Hz as read from a longer Results sentence) and the Discussion gives a third figure for 8000 Hz, so the paper is not fully consistent; Table 1 per-owl values not read; sound-field calibration at the owl's head not read

source.authors: Bianca Krumm, Georg M. Klump, Christine Köppl, Ulrike Langemann
source.title: The barn owls' Minimum Audible Angle

quote: With BB noise, the MAA further decreased to 4.9° ± 0.3°.
note: Family and order from the US Fish and Wildlife Service taxonomic tree entry for Tyto alba (the paper names the genus and species only). Crossref licence CC BY 4.0, vor, issued 2019-08-23; the page prints the Creative Commons Attribution License. The quote is the whole sentence as returned by the page tool; BB is the paper's abbreviation for broadband noise. No value for frequency-specific MAA is filed because those sentences exceed the tool limit.

value: two foveae: central fovea 217.66 um deep, temporal fovea 106.38 um deep
method: histology: paraffin sections (4 um) of a fixed eye, depth measured on the section with maximum foveal depth (Fiji)
conditions: two adult male kestrels (161.23 g and 179.56 g) from a wildlife recovery centre, euthanised on veterinary grounds after severe injury; the foveal depths are single representative values from one eye (which bird not stated), with no variance or replicate; tissue fixed in 4% paraformaldehyde for 2 h, dehydrated in ethanol, cleared in xylene and paraffin-embedded, with no shrinkage correction or discussion of shrinkage; the central fovea is described as deep convexiclivate within the area centralis and the temporal fovea as a deep pit with steep walls (foveal widths 393.08 um and 265.95 um); S- and L/M-opsin immunoreactivity was found in both foveae and rhodopsin was absent from the central foveal pit; the temporal fovea is called shallow in earlier papers cited on main, here it is about half the depth of the central one

source.authors: Raúl Cobo, Daniela Jiménez-Díaz, Alicia Navarro-Sempere, Magdalena García, Yolanda Segovia
source.title: Eye Morphology, Foveal Structure and Photoreceptor Composition in Both Foveae of Common Kestrel (Falco tinnunculus Linnaeus, 1758)

quote: The central and temporal foveae exhibited depths of 217.66 µm and 106.38 µm, respectively.
note: Family and order as on main for the Falco rows. Crossref licence CC BY 4.0, vor, issued 2026-06-17; the page metadata gives CC BY 3.0 (filed as CC BY). The page metadata lists Segovia first but the byline and Crossref list Cobo first; byline order used. Foveal depth only; no cone or ganglion-cell density is printed in the Abstract or Results.

value: nine EAG-active compounds, all cuticular hydrocarbons, found by GC-EAD
method: gas chromatography with electroantennographic detection (GC-EAD) of cuticular washes; a compound counted as EAG-active if it elicited a response in at least three successful recordings
conditions: field-collected adults from two Lithuanian forests (Sept-Oct 2014-2017), held at about 4 C for 6-8 days before washing; 11 male and 12 female antennae; the Results state that male-derived washes gave nine EAG-active compounds and female-derived washes six (read from a Results fragment), so the Abstract's nine refers to one wash type; the strongest male antennal responses were to n-pentacosane and (Z)-9-pentacosene (Abstract fragment); a hexane solvent control was used in the behavioural assay (8-12 males per treatment, each male tested once; Mann-Whitney U); no EAG amplitudes in mV were read; enantiomers of 3-methylheneicosane described as novel olfactory and behavioural findings in insects

source.authors: Vincas Būda, Violeta Apšegaitė, Laima Blažytė-Čereškienė, Sigitas Podėnas, João Pedro de A. Souza, Paulo H. G. Zarbin, Linas Labanauskas, Tomas Paškevičius, Vilma Baužienė, Sandra Radžiutė
source.title: Pheromones in Crane Flies: Behaviorally Active Cuticular Compounds in Tipula autumnalis Loew (Diptera: Tipulidae)
